chunks: It is reported from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The height of the Kaaba in those days was nine cubits, and there was no roof for it. So the Quraysh placed a roof on it of eighteen cubits. Then it did not cease to be so, until al-Hajjaj demolished it in his campaign against Ibn al-Zubayr, and rebuilt it and made it twenty-seven cubits.

key_terms.أَذْرُع / ذِرَاع: Cubit — a unit of measurement approximately equal to the length of a forearm (roughly 45-55 cm)
key_terms.الْحَجَّاج: Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi, the notorious Umayyad governor of Iraq
key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Kaaba — the cubic sacred shrine at the center of the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What was the original height of the Kaaba and how did it change historically according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the architectural history of the Kaaba, describing how its height changed over time: originally nine cubits with no roof, expanded by the Quraysh to eighteen cubits, and later rebuilt by al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf to twenty-seven cubits after demolishing it during the conflict with Ibn al-Zubayr (692 CE). This hadith provides historical context about the physical structure of Islam's most sacred site and its modifications through history.

en.hubeali:
And it is reported from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Aban Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The height of the Kaaba in those days used to be of nine cubits, and there did not happen to be a roof for it. So the Qureysh placed a roof on it of eighteen cubits. Then it did not cease to be so, until Al-Hajjaj broke it down upon (in his fight against) Ibn Al-Zubeyr, and made it to be of twenty seven cubits’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from ibn abu Nasr from Aban ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the height of al-Ka‘bah in those days was nine yards and it did not have a roof. Quraysh made a roof for it with height of eighteen yards, with which it remained until Hajjaj destroyed it on (during his fight with) ibn al-Zubayr. He rebuilt it and made it twenty-seven yards high.’”
